title: Fatter Tracker
tagline: Our phones keep the game straight. A tiny printer makes the missing tokens.
what: A shared Magic: The Gathering game table I built for my friends. Everybody's phone stays on the same life totals, poison, damage and turn clock, and a web button prints any card token we need during the game.
built: Synced life, poison and commander damage for two to six players across their phones in real time
Added game codes, a lobby, per-player chess clocks, history and win-rate profiles
Reverse-engineered the printer's Bluetooth sign-in and its request to resend a lost packet
Turned card art into a dithered, one-bit, 384-dot print with its own calibration strip

making.problem: A Commander table has too many totals for one person to babysit, and the tiny printer on the table only worked through its vendor phone app.
how: One game code puts two to six phones in the same live game
Every life, poison, damage and turn change is sent to the whole table
The token page finds the card art, shrinks it to the printer's 384 dots and dithers it to black or white
The printer signs in over Bluetooth and reports any packet it needs again

broke.title: The print that stopped halfway
broke.body: The printer was asking for one lost packet, so I taught the sender to rewind to that packet and finish the card.

credits: Card data and art come from Scryfall

moment.what: In the middle of a game, I can search a card on the web page and the 48 mm printer spits out its 384-dot token without the vendor app.
